selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with acute urinary retention, hematemesis, progressive neurological deficits, and marked paraparesis, along with the presence of multiple bilateral symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions in the brain and diffuse T2 hyperintensities throughout the spinal cord, is most consistent with Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis (ADEM). The lack of albuminocytologic dissociation and the presence of normal sensory function also support this diagnosis. While Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD) is a close runner-up due to the involvement of the spinal cord and brainstem, the presence of multiple symmetrical lesions and the lack of optic neuritis or area postrema syndrome make ADEM a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.why: While the patient has spinal cord involvement, the presence of multiple bilateral symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions in the brain is not consistent with Acute Transverse Myelitis.
